audit.whatIsWrong: All seven chart rows disagreed across layers: phases[0..5].side read 'Skill' and phases[6].side read 'Yasuo', while win[0..6] read LeBlanc, LeBlanc, LeBlanc, LeBlanc, LeBlanc, Yasuo, LeBlanc.
audit.why: packet.levelChart matches the content layer exactly, so the full-layer sides are the stale copy. The page currently renders two different answers to who wins every single stage.
audit.corrected: All seven phases[N].side moved onto the packet/content values, proposed as one atomic group, and phases[5].why rewritten so the sentence agrees with the new Yasuo verdict.

audit.whatIsWrong: Wind Wall was called a 'fifteen-second invitation'.
audit.why: Wind Wall is 25/23/21/19/17s and lasts 4 seconds. At rank 1 that is a 25-second window, not fifteen — the number changes when you commit.
audit.corrected: Real cooldowns written into breakdown.cooldowns and breakdown.feeding; Steel Tempest's 4s and Last Breath's 70s added.

audit.whatIsWrong: The page said Wind Wall blocks 'your Chaos Orb' — a fabricated ability name attached to the wrong ability.
audit.why: The projectile flag in your kit sits on Ethereal Chains (E, 925 range, 14s at rank 1), not on the Q sigil. Wind Wall blocks all enemy projectiles for 4 seconds, so the ability it actually deletes is your chain — which is your entire engage and your only lockdown. Getting this wrong tells the reader to bait the wall for the wrong spell.
audit.corrected: Wind Wall vs Ethereal Chains stated in breakdown.cooldowns, spikes[1], mid, wants.you[1] and wants.foe[1].

audit.why: Wind Wall's 25s at rank 1 is the whole timing problem of this lane.
audit.corrected: Rewritten with Wind Wall 25s/17s, Steel Tempest 4s, Last Breath 70s.

edits.before: First item spike: Q-W-RW deletes squishies. Spend the lane lead before scaling lanes wake.
edits.after: His first crit item lands and Steel Tempest starts hurting on a 4s cooldown. Poke and leave; do not sign a second round.

edits.before: - Yasuo Wind Wall: matchup-defining — Blocks every projectile for its duration — hold your poke until it is spent. Read it like a second minimap. - Guard your W Distortion (return) like a fifth summoner spell. - Ultimate goes to kill windows only.
edits.after: - Wind Wall (W): 25s at rank 1, 17s at rank 5, up for 4 seconds — it eats Ethereal Chains outright, so chain only after it drops. Count it. - Steel Tempest is 4s and knocks up on the second stack. - Last Breath is 70s at rank 1.

edits.before: Q the sigil, W the detonation, return before the answer — a half-bar round trip he experienced as weather.
edits.after: Sweeping Blade is 0.5s but cannot re-hit the same target — chain him at the far end, where he has nothing left to dash off.

edits.before: Yasuo burns Wind Wall on nothing — take the fifteen-second invitation.
edits.after: Mimic your Distortion, not your chain — the wall eats chains, never a dash.

edits.before: That’s Yasuo’s bread-and-butter play — deny it and they run out of answers.
edits.after: His passive shield builds as he walks and eats your opener — the maths lie.

edits.before: Staying at the W landing spot for one more auto — the return timer is your champion; outliving it is optional.
edits.after: Each melee exchange feeds Steel Tempest on 4 seconds and a passive shield he stacked by walking — that range is his.

edits.before: Yasuo wins by landing Wind Wall, denying your pattern, and turning your every misstep into the all-in you hadn’t budgeted.
edits.after: Yasuo wins by walling your chain, closing with Sweeping Blade, and turning one missed step into a knockup and Last Breath.

edits.before: Carry through picks — one chained carry per objective; your job is the flank angle and the discipline to leave after.
edits.after: Carry through picks — chain him from behind, where the wall is already pointing the wrong way; it covers one line only.

edits.before: If Yasuo opens the score, reset expectations and respect Wind Wall doubly. After a second, your job description changes — farm with W clears and stay relevant through chain picks.
edits.after: If Yasuo opens the score, stop chaining into a wall you haven't counted — 25 seconds at rank 1. After a second kill: W-clear, never stand inside his 475 range, and take your picks off-lane.

edits.before: At 6 Yasuo's Last Breath combined with a jungler or support knockup threatens to delete you instantly, and his Wind Wall can block your Chaos Orb, flipping the all-in against you if he catches the engage timing.
edits.after: At 6 Yasuo's Last Breath combined with a jungler or support knockup threatens to delete you instantly, and Wind Wall eats Ethereal Chains outright, flipping the all-in against you if he catches the engage timing.

edits.before: Levels 3-5 you still win clean trades and all-ins, but level 6 flips briefly — his Last Breath combined with any external knockup threatens an instant burst on you, and Wind Wall can eat your Chaos Orb if timed well, so avoid committing your all-in blind right at 6. Bait Wind Wall from max range first, then engage once it's down.
edits.after: Levels 3-5 you still win clean trades and all-ins, but level 6 flips briefly — his Last Breath combined with any external knockup threatens an instant burst on you, and Wind Wall eats Ethereal Chains for its full 4 seconds, so never open blind at 6. Bait the wall from outside his 400 range first, then engage once it's down.

edits.before: Bait Wind Wall before landing Chaos Orb
edits.after: Bait Wind Wall before landing Ethereal Chains

edits.before: Wind Wall your key poke or engage ability
edits.after: Wind Wall your Ethereal Chains engage

notes: CHART: all seven rows disagreed across layers. packet.levelChart and the content win[] array are identical, so I moved the full-layer phases[N].side onto them as one atomic group rather than touching win[N] — the content layer already holds the correct values, so there is no matching win[N] edit to pair (a no-op edit is not proposable). phases[5].why was rewritten in the same proposal so the sentence agrees with the new Yasuo verdict; phases[6].why already described LeBlanc winning. Ratings left untouched deliberately: the rating semantics are inconsistent across this champion's pages (LeBlanc-side stages run 8/10 on some matchups, Yasuo-side 7/10 here) and I could not tell from the data whether the number is owner-perspective, so guessing would inject a new error.
